therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: Adenosine A2a receptor antagonism combined with PD-1 checkpoint inhibition
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: Reversal of adenosine-mediated immunosuppression in tumor microenvironment combined with T-cell activation via PD-1 blockade
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Patients with solid tumors (NSCLC, RCC, pancreatic, urothelial, head and neck, TNBC, melanoma, mCRPC) and DLBCL
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Overall Response Rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 for solid tumors and Cheson 2014 for DLBCL

results.effect_size: ORR ranged from 0% to 27.3% across tumor types, with highest responses in RCC naïve (27.3% at 160mg, 25.0% at 240mg)
results.target_engagement_evidence: PK data showed dose-proportional exposure for NIR178 with accumulation at steady state. CD8+ T-cell infiltration increased in some tumor types (RCC naïve: 10.93%, TNBC: 4.86%)
biomarker_changes: Increased CD8+ T-cell infiltration in RCC naïve (10.93% and 10.53% for 160mg and 240mg)
Minimal changes in most other tumor types
subgroup_findings: Best responses in RCC treatment-naïve patients
Minimal activity in MSS colorectal cancer
Limited activity in NSCLC across all dosing schedules
safety_signals: Treatment-related AEs common across all cohorts
results.dose_information: NIR178: 80, 160, or 240 mg BID orally; PDR001: 400 mg IV Q4W. Multiple dosing schedules tested: continuous, 2wk-on/2wk-off, 1wk-on/1wk-off
